claims.finding: For C in G, query C parentclock, the G tail-DSP clock; start and fade coordinates use that domain.
Fade points are linear between specified points and scale against other volume settings. No endpoint-outside transfer function inferred.
Explicit target group and paused creation permit setup before audibility; later local unpause does not override parent pause.
A nonblocking handle is not readiness; wait for READY. Scoped method uses already prepared memory samples, not streaming starvation handling.
Clock propagation defaults true. Releasing group reroutes inputs to master; fixed ownership and routing are preconditions, not an arbitrary clock conversion algorithm.
Opt zero ignores optional argument; scoped start scheduling does not set an end target.
Local pause flags and effective ancestor pause differ; pitch/rate and pause mean clock distance is not a universal wall/device interval.
Manual reverb pulling before owner-group scheduling can expose a second path; order or SEND remedy has conditions, including one-block wet delay if reverb still executes first.
Stopped/naturally-ended Channel handles become invalid. Failed preparation must not continue using invalid handles.
Paused creation, parent clock, future fades and same-start delay, then unpause. Historical two-block lead suggestion is not a universal current guarantee.
Positive intervals, overflow checks, return-value gates, reserve recheck and abandon-if-late policy are explicit application design, not native past-target behavior or atomic commit guarantee.
